aggressive_definition: Aggressive prostate cancer defined as Gleason sum ≥7 or clinical stage III or IV disease.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: aggressive (Gleason sum > or = 7 or clinical stage III or IV) disease
study_design: Prospective nested case-control study within the PLCO Cancer Screening Trial.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: The study included 749 case patients with incident prostate cancer who were diagnosed 1-8 years after blood draw and 781 control subjects who were frequency matched by age at cohort entry, time since initial screening, and calendar year of cohort entry.
reason: The nested case-control analysis evaluated overall incident prostate cancer and explicitly defined and analyzed aggressive incident disease among men whose blood was collected before diagnosis.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: However, serum 25(OH)D concentrations greater than the lowest quintile (Q1) were associated with increased risk of aggressive (Gleason sum > or = 7 or clinical stage III or IV) disease (in a model adjusting for matching factors, study center, and history of diabetes, ORs for Q2 vs Q1 = 1.20, 95% CI = 0.80 to 1.81, for Q3 vs Q1 =1.96, 95% CI = 1.34 to 2.87, for Q4 vs Q1 = 1.61, 95% CI = 1.09 to 2.38, and for Q5 vs Q1 = 1.37, 95% CI = 0.92 to 2.05; P(trend) = .05).
estimate_classifications.reason: The row's Q3-versus-Q1 OR and confidence interval are explicitly reported for the defined aggressive endpoint.

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
